cohort: The study included 120 women who had experienced either a stillbirth (N=57) or an early miscarriage (N=63).
finding: Mothers who experienced stillbirth exhibited significantly higher levels of posttraumatic growth, posttraumatic stress, perinatal grief, disclosure, challenge to assumptive beliefs, and rumination compared to mothers who experienced early miscarriage.
cross-section timing: 2 to 6 years after the pregnancy loss event
